Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The death of Jade Panayiotou has made headlines since she first disappeared and an alarm was raised on social media. We look at the trial in which her husband, Christopher is a murder suspect.

Unique Selling Point:
The death of Jade Panayiotou has made headlines since she first disappeared and an alarm was raised on social media by a teacher who worked with her and drove to school with her every morning.
When her body was found some time later, a lot of pieces in the puzzle were missing.
As the pieces slowly started to trickle in, a lot of things became much clearer.
When her husband, Christopher was apprehended some time later, a lot of people were stunned as to how the the pieces of the puzzle fit together.
We look at the trial in which her husband, Christopher is a murder suspect.

Summary:
Christopher has applied for bail more than twice. It was denied in all cases.
The hitman that he allegedly got to murder Jade, passed away while in incarceration in a hospital shortly before the trial started.
More than eighteen months after her death, Jade's family is still overwhelmed with grief. All they want is justice for Jade.
Christopher's family has been mum - not speaking to the media, but supporting him at court every day.
The trial started on the 11th of October and is on the roll until the 2nd of December.
We take a look at what has been testified so far.

Press Release:


Panayiotou Trial: Week 3
More than a year after Jayde Panayiotou's death, the Port Elizabeth High Court is hearing the details of her final few hours - but not without controversy. In a Carte Blanche exclusive, close friend and confidante Cherise Swanepoel and sister Toni Inggs speak candidly about Jayde’s disappearance and subsequent murder.


Script:


PANAYIOTOU TRIAL I SCRIPT

PRODUCER: ESTÉ DE KLERK

PRESENTER: JOHN WEBB

EDITOR: PETER GROENEWALD

BROADCAST DATE: 30 OCTOBER 2016

Eighteen months ago, a well-loved teacher from the Riebeek College Girls High School in Uitenhage in the Eastern Cape went missing.
Jayde Panayiotou was 29-years old when she disappeared on the morning of 21 April 2015.
The community where she grew up was galvanized immediately in frantic search of her (shots from community getting together in previous story)– physically and through social media.
Three shots were heard on that morning in a barren area near the township of KwaNoBuhle, the police were informed and launched a search.
But when her body was found the next morning, shock and outrage were palpable.
She’d been murdered… after she was kidnapped outside her townhouse complex in Port Elizabeth while she waited for her closest friend and colleague to collect her before school.

JOHN LINK: This is the area outside KwaNoBuhle where the kidnappers brought Jayde and where she took her final breath. Driving from Port Elizabeth, what immediately springs to mind is how much time she would have had trapped in the boot, thinking about her fate.

CHERISE SWANEPOEL: The first words I could get out of my mouth was: “I’m sorry.” Even on the day she went missing I kept saying ‘I am sorry’. I felt like I should have been there for her.

Cherise Swanepoel was Jayde’s closest friend and they shared a car-pool to school every day. In an exclusive interview this week, she told us nothing could have prepared her for the news of Jayde’s death.

CHERISE SWANEPOEL: my mind was telling me brace yourself and my heart was saying .. they going to say they found her and she is okay. I just remember falling to the ground and saying No .

Jayde was laid to rest a week after her death (footage/pics of Jayde’s funeral from previous story) and her husband Christopher delivered a moving tribute.
A breakthrough was made in days when two suspects were arrested – Luthando Siyoni and Jayde’s husband, Christopher.

JOHN: I know that you don’t want to talk about Chris and we need to respect that. How did you react when he was arrested?

CHERISE SWANEPOEL: There was disbelief and that there was some form of mistake. It was kind of like losing two people at once.

During the course of the next year, three more suspects were arrested. Christopher has been languishing at St Albans prison since his arrest. He was initially denied bail in the Port Elizabeth Magistrate’s Court and again in the Grahamstown High Court when he appealed that decision. In May, his third attempt to apply for bail on new facts, also failed.
The trial started on October, 11th.

JOHN LINK: COURT: It’s been an emotional three weeks in the Panayiotou trial, understandably, given that eighteen months after Jayde’s murder, and given understandably, her friends and family have had to relive her final moments.

Pivotal to the trial is a letter Jayde wrote seven months before she died – found by her younger sister, Toni Inggs after Jayde was murdered.

JAYDE LETTER: “All I have ever wanted was to be loved fully and completely… I am not an unrealistic person…, but I don’t feel the love I dream about.
“Why am I not the apple of my husband’s eye? Why does he hide so much from me and why is it impossible to communicate with him? Why do I feel like I have to constantly compete with him or to be seen by him? Why will he never apologise when he is wrong? Why did he break his promise to me?”

This letter – so telling of what Jayde was feeling, particularly in relation to her husband, Christopher - was read into the court record when Toni took the stand.
In an exclusive interview with us this week, she said she stays strong for her mom and dad, and especially in memory of Jayde.

JOHN: Are those accurate reflections of how she was feeling at the time, would you say?

TONI INGGS: I would say so yes. Me and her share a very similar thing there where I cannot always voice how I feel but will write it down.

JOHN: And how was she feeling, do you think?

TONI: Lonely… for a long time …

Cherise echoed what Toni said.

CHERISE SWANEPOEL: There were many times she couldn’t speak about how lonely she was. I was never going to force it on the stand and if that came up then it came up … but I knew I could be a voice for her. In a way I said things I MANAGED to say a couple of things wish I had said when she was still here … she is lonely just spend some time with her.

JOHN: Was that something she expressed to you?

CHERISE SWANEPOEL: Ja, often. There was no secret she was alone and there was no secret that she was lonely and I know those are two different things, but she felt them both.

The State alleges that Christopher had used the cellphone of a former handyman at his nightclub and the family’s OK Grocer – state witness Mawonga Ndedwa to contact middleman, Luthando Siyoni, a bouncer at the nightclub.
Christopher allegedly inquired from Siyoni whether he could have a person killed on his behalf.
The State alleges it was Siyoni who then recruited gunman Sizwe Vumazonke, Sinethemba Nemembe and co-conspirator Zolani Sibeko.
Siyoni, arrested a week after the murder, supplied the police with an alleged version of events which turned their focus on Christopher. Siyoni has since turned state witness.

The three accused pleaded not guilty on all charges, including conspiracy to murder and kidnapping – and Vumazonke died in September.

JOHN LINK: The State’s case hasn’t been helped by the death of the gunman, Sizwe Vumazonke, but given the circumstances of his death, the state has called for a toxicology report to determine whether or not he was poisoned.

In Christopher’s plea explanation, read by his advocate, Terry Price SC, he said: “I deny that played any role whatsoever in the death of my wife, Jayde. I do not know any of my fellow accused and have never met or heard of them prior to being arrested in this case. Jayde and I…as far as I was concerned, we were happily married”.
However, state witness, Clarishka Kapp testified that Christopher had had an affair with her friend, Chanelle Coutts, since before he married Jayde.

JOHN TO TONI: What is it like walking into court every morning?

TONI: every morning is a roller coaster of emotions and anxiety.

JOHN: When you say that you are anxious, are you anxious because of people watching you or of what you might hear?

TONI: I think it is because of what I might hear .. the truth hurts unfortunately.

JOHN LINK: alongside that emotional testimony has been some fairly technical evidence which once again has cast the spotlight on the role of the police.

There are allegations of Siyoni and Vumazonke being assaulted, the wrong dates on witness statements, and state witness – Siyoni’s girlfriend, Babalwa Breakfast being declared a hostile witness on Thursday, because her testimony refuted two statements she made to the police. Shortly after her testimony, Breakfast was arrested and charged with perjury and defeating the ends of justice.

KATHRYN KIMBERLEY: She told us that money she found in his gym bag .. he told her it was meant for renovations at his gym.. Previously we had heard in court that at all times she was aware that the money was used for hitmen to kill Jayde.

Kathryn Kimberley is a senior reporter at the PE Herald.

JOHN: What have you been able to make of the police investigation in this case?

KATHRYN KIMBERLEY: We’ve heard from one of the police officers where an injury to one of the accused wasn’t filled in properly in the occurrence book. Another instance with Vumazonke, the alleged trigger man, how he sustained that injury it also not written in correctly it, but the policeman signed next to it. He said it was human error.

According to the state, the initial plan was to kill Jayde on the 5th of April 2015, and that Christopher handed over money to Siyoni to hire a car two weeks prior to Jayde’s kidnapping and murder to follow Jayde and Cherise.
Cherise provided a timeline to the court that indicated that the kidnapping in front of Jayde’s complex happened in under nine minutes.

CHERISE: I remember messaging her from the fuel station to say: “I am just putting in fuel…” I think that was at 20 past 6 that day. I think it was three or four minutes later I said on my way. Nine minutes later I arrived at the gate and messaged to say I am here. That message never went through. I tried to call a couple of times and her phone was off.

Cherise testified how she and Christopher started to search for Jayde immediately.

CHERISE: We got in his car and started looking for her … and drove around the block and happened upon a police van. Told them we were looking for Jayde.

JOHN: In that moment, how would you describe Chris’s frame of mind?

CHERISE: Like I said on the stand he was determined to find her … so was I - we all were.

JOHN LINK: The police ballistics expert testified that Jayde was shot twice in the back before falling over. The gunman then leaned over her and fired the fatal shot to her head. The body was discovered the next day in an area just behind me.

The forensic pathalogist testified that gun-powder was found on Jayde’s left hand and it seemed as if she was trying to shield away from the gunman.

JOHN: On the stand, the answer you gave was that you are angry 90% of the time?

TONI: I have become a lot more angry person .. deal with every situation angry perspective. Usually happy. I think that until end off trial I will be who I am.

JOHN: When you say you are angry at?

TONI: Just whoever was involved I am angry with them and angry they felt they could play God.

Christopher alleges the State came to court with “dirty hands” and that “the evidence against him was obtained unlawfully and his right to a fair trial has been violated”.
The defence has requested a trial within a trial, saying all information obtained from Siyoni – after the police removed him from Christopher’s nightclub - should be ruled inadmissible.

KATHRYN: the defense is alleging he was beaten up and forced into implicating Christopher. They are using the fruit of a poison tree approach. They are saying that everything after that point should be inadmissible. The state will should try and get all that evidence admitted and have him called as a witness.

The case is on the roll until December the 2nd, but it’s uncertain whether judgment will be handed down this year.
However, for those closest to Jayde – and Christopher – the trial couldn’t wrap up soon enough.
And it’s perhaps this paragraph in Jayde’s letter that sums up her inner hurt most…

JAYDE’S LETTER: “I feel as if I don’t have a heart. It is torn and shredded and full of holes.The aura of my being is slow-fading. The spark within is burning out. No more longing for the future, the soul is worn-out.”

CHERISE: Up until last week when a photo on the scene a part of me thought she was still alive. Then you realize that and reality hits you’re really hard when there is evidence she is no longer here.


-------END--------

PROMOS

PROMO 1: 15”

CHERISE: reality hits you’re really hard when there is evidence she is no longer here.

Insight into the Panayiotou trial. We speak to Jayde’s closest friend and sister - exclusively.

PROMO 2: 15”

JOHN: how was she feeling, do you think?

TONI: Lonely… for a long time …

Insight into the Panayiotou trial. We speak to Jayde’s sister and closest friend - exclusively.

PROMO 3: 10”

CHERISE: reality hits you’re really hard when there is evidence she is no longer here.

We bring you insight into the Panayiotou trial.

The defence has requested a trial within a trial, saying all information obtained from Siyoni – after the police removed him from Christopher’s nightclub - should be ruled inadmissible. KATHRYN: the defense is alleging he was beaten up and forced into implicating Christopher. They are using the fruit of a poison tree approach. They are saying that everything after that point should be inadmissible. The state will should try and get all that evidence admitted and have him called as a witness. The case is on the roll until December the 2nd, but it’s uncertain whether judgment will be handed down this year. However, for those closest to Jayde – and Christopher – the trial couldn’t wrap up soon enough. And it’s perhaps this paragraph in Jayde’s letter that sums up her inner hurt most… JAYDE’S LETTER: “I feel as if I don’t have a heart. It is torn and shredded and full of holes.The aura of my being is slow-fading. The spark within is burning out. No more longing for the future, the soul is worn-out.” CHERISE: Up until last week when a photo on the scene a part of me thought she was still alive. Then you realize that and reality hits you’re really hard when there is evidence she is no longer here. -------END-------- PROMOS PROMO 1: 15” CHERISE: reality hits you’re really hard when there is evidence she is no longer here. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The death of Jade Panayiotou has made headlines since she first disappeared and an alarm was raised on social media. We look at the trial in which her husband, Christopher is a murder suspect.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The death of Jade Panayiotou has made headlines since she first disappeared and an alarm was raised on social media by a teacher who worked with her and drove to school with her every morning. When her body was found some time later, a lot of pieces in the puzzle were missing. As the pieces slowly started to trickle in, a lot of things became much clearer. When her husband, Christopher was apprehended some time later, a lot of people were stunned as to how the the pieces of the puzzle fit together. We look at the trial in which her husband, Christopher is a murder suspect.
metadata.Summary: Christopher has applied for bail more than twice. It was denied in all cases. The hitman that he allegedly got to murder Jade, passed away while in incarceration in a hospital shortly before the trial started. More than eighteen months after her death, Jade's family is still overwhelmed with grief. All they want is justice for Jade. Christopher's family has been mum - not speaking to the media, but supporting him at court every day. The trial started on the 11th of October and is on the roll until the 2nd of December. We take a look at what has been testified so far.
